newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares close higher on budget cut.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares close higher on budget cut.

text.p: Israeli shares closed broadly higher on Wednesday as investors' mood improved on the Dow's rise and the budget cut, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares gained 1.33 percent, or 3.89 points, to 297.32 on an all-share turnover of 176 million shekels against 149 million shekels on Monday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.36 percent higher at 304.17.
"The rise of Wall Street after Greenspan's testimony was the main reason for the optimistic opening," said Daniel Werker-Barak at Ofek Securities.
Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony on the U.S. economy drove the Dow Jones Industrial Average to a record close on Tuesday.
"The market was also affected by the approval of the budget cuts and the successful talks with the Palestinians," Werker-Barak said.
The Israeli cabinet approved on Wednesday a 800 million shekel cut in the 1997 budget. The cuts were the third round of budget slashing since the draft 1997 budget was presented last autumn.

Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat fell out diplomatically on Wednesday over whether their meeting on Tuesday had broken the logjam in the Middle East peace process.
Arafat said the meeting had achieved nothing, while Levi said it had given new impetus to the talks.
"Everything looks much better. Wall Street rose, the government slashed the budget and even the talks with the Palestinians have resumed," said a trader at United Mizrahi Bank.
Traders said the market is expected to open with surplus supply on Thursday as options players may dump shares on their expiry date in order to lower the Maof index.

"The Maof players were trying to push the market downward today but they did not succeed. Thursday is their last chance," the Mizrahi trader said. Koor Industries, the most active share, fell 2.5 percent to 37,404 agorot on volume of 16.9 million shekels.
Claridge Israel said on Tuesday it had bought 10 percent of Koor from Shamrock Holdings with an option to buy another 10 percent within 90 days.
Claridge, an investment company controlled by the Charles Bronfman family of Canada, paid approximately $185 million for the stake.
"Koor is fully priced now and in the short term there is no reason to buy the share," Warker said.

Other active shares include Bank Leumi which rose 3.5 percent to 571 agorot on volume of 12 million shekels; and Bezeq Israel Telecom, which fell 0.75 to 993 agorot on turnover of 15.4 million shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233 DMG SAS
